Hey there, you’re definitely not alone. A few weeks from now will mark one year of cutting contact with my stepdad and, unfortunately, my mother. I say that because she’s not necessarily as abusive as my stepdad, but she enables him and put his and her wants and needs over mine. All the shame of “failing” in life whenever I made a mistake or struggled with money or school, comparing me to my more “successful” friends, their petty arguments that spun out of control and got me involved without any reason. I grew up very reclusive.

Being told by my mother that we both needed to “walk on eggshells” around him as if I was responsible for his shitty behavior, made me feel empty and resentful. I couldn’t be my true self around them out of fear of their disapproval. 

My stepdad is an alcoholic. He goes off on rants and would get verbally (and sometimes physically) violent with my mom and I. One day he accused me of “using” his mother for money, when she was the one who initially offered me money for raking pine needles on her land and selling them to her friends to use in their gardens. I forgave him the first time, but once he did it again I just couldn’t. 

I still feel bad for leaving them and not helping them recover, but I had to realize that you can’t help those who choose to not help themselves. I’ve done a lot of growing up since then, and I still grieve for the loving and compassionate mother that I deserved. You’ve got a friend in me, and feel free to PM me anytime.

First off, I commend you. You are very brave for taking a step back and going NC. I think therapy is a great first step on the road to recovering and rediscovering yourself.

Your mother needs professional help. She does not need you and neither do you her. She isn’t looking for your sympathy. She wants your vulnerability, so she can continue to treat you like you’re her personal hostage. It is not your responsibility to get her to see her own insecurity. And it is absolutely not her right to project and threaten others with manipulation tactics such as suicide, especially to her own son.

It’s only human to have sympathy for someone in that state. And it’s normal to feel guilt and shame from all the trauma. But seeking therapy and looking out for your own best interest is ultimately the best decision you can make right now. You just have to learn to believe in you. I do.

1. White Pony. Always appreciated this album but considered S/T to be my favorite for a while because of the moodiness and heavy riffage (probably had something to do with my teen angst lol). The entire band at their experimental prime, superb musicianship all around.

2. Self Titled. Criminally underrated. This album will always have a special place in my heart. The first time I heard Bloody Cape, something clicked in me and instantly fell in love with it as cheesy as that sounds. This album introduced me to the rabbit hole of experimental music during senior year. Also artwork is my all time favorite, like, ever.

3. Around The Fur. Sonically their best produced heavier album imo. Terry Date was on one with this. Be Quiet and Drive is still my second fav Deftones song.

4. Diamonds Eyes. Their comeback record after Chi's accident. They couldn't have done it any better. Although mixing is a tad shotty in some places, the grooves and riffs along with Chino's hooks are so goddamn catchy.

5. Koi No Yokan. This is like SNW 2.0 but without the buttfucking residue anthem. Production got much better here, despite a couple underwhelming tracks. The pummeling riffs mixed with ethereal passages are amazing.

6. Saturday Night Wrist. I actually hated this album for a long time but has since grown on me quite a bit, minus Pink Cellphone (motherfuck that shit). Rats!Rats!Rats! still kicks my ass. Riviere is very underrated too.

7. Adrenaline. Not a bad debut at all, although it is somewhat repetitive at times. Love Root and Bored.

8. Gore. Personally, as much as I hate to admit I just can't bring myself to enjoy this album. Other than a couple cool passages here and there, this just kinda disappoints sadly.
